name: plate-45-board-daynums
version_tag: #143 BOARD DAY NUMBERS — 1-31 white-in-black, TWO COLOUR. Ron: white date numbers so he can see how to set the mechanism. REQUIRES the two-filament change to compose_plate.py (same commit): the config the composer hands the slicer stores per-extruder values as slot-indexed lists, and canonical_config leaves every one of them at length 1 — declare a second colour without widening them and the slicer silently prints the whole plate in slot 1. _add_second_filament widens them and sets slot 2's identity; a new gate refuses any plate that declares two filaments but whose GCODE only ever loads one slot (that failure looks correct in preview). AMS: slot 1 black, slot 2 WHITE — check the ams_mapping in the start payload before confirming, this is the first plate where tray order matters. GEOMETRY: the date convention is taken from the simulator's underside pin crown, not invented — date = (steps mod 31)+1, so date d sits at board-frame 90deg - (d-1)x11.613deg with digits' up radially outward, and the number at the reading index (world 90, 12 o'clock) is the current date. A witness notch outboard of date 1 confirms the ring's clocking at a glance. Numbers are cut into BOTH faces (0.8mm deep, 2.4mm solid core between): the three satellites are carried BY the board so their shadow is fixed in board frame and covers dates 3-9 at ANY radius — the mirrored underside ring is the only way to read those seven. Recessed rather than cut through because a through-cut strands the counters of 0/4/6/8/9 as floating islands (the gate found 26). Measured: tightest adjacent-number gap 1.46mm, outermost glyph r35.52 vs gear root 37.05 (1.53mm margin), no overlaps. REGISTRATION: compose centres each object on its own bbox, and these two differ — the white part's position carries a deliberate [-0.051, +0.389] offset. Do not 'tidy' it to match the board. 2 parts, flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06. | QUIET.
